title: Cyclone Akvan Veers North and Weakens; Landfall Window Now Narsapur to Puri
excerpt: The IMD's revised forecast moves the November 20 landfall zone into Odisha's reach, cuts the expected intensity to a severe cyclonic storm, and puts 10 Andhra Pradesh districts on rain alert.
body:
• The India Meteorological Department (IMD) now expects severe cyclonic storm Akvan to cross the north Andhra Pradesh-Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by noon on Friday, November 20 — a landfall zone shifted well north of its earlier Nellore-Visakhapatnam forecast in less than a day.
  • The storm has also weakened against the earlier forecast: it is now expected to remain a severe cyclonic storm at landfall, with winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph, instead of intensifying into a very severe cyclonic storm, and forecasters do not rule out further weakening in the next 24 hours.
  • Extremely heavy rainfall is likely on November 19 and 20 in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli and Kakinada districts, with an orange alert for Parvathipuram Manyam, Konaseema, East Godavari and West Godavari; a storm surge of 0.5 to 1 metre above the tide could inundate low-lying areas of south coastal Odisha.
  • For residents in the alert districts: the IMD's own forecasters say their models are disagreeing unusually sharply on this storm, so the exact landfall point remains uncertain — follow district administration and IMD updates, with more clarity expected by Wednesday night.

Severe cyclonic storm Akvan changed track in less than a day, veering away from the Machilipatnam area towards north coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a fresh bulletin on Wednesday with a revised landfall zone and new rainfall alerts, The Hindu reported.

The IMD now expects Akvan to cross the north Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha by noon on November 20, as a severe cyclonic storm with maximum sustained winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph, according to Sambad English's report of the IMD forecast. The department's earlier forecast had the storm crossing the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, and intensifying further before landfall.

Where the storm is

At 8:30 a.m. on Wednesday, the system over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal was moving slowly north-northwestwards and lay about 570 km east of Chennai, 580 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 590 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 660 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 710 km south of Gopalpur and 770 km south of Puri, the IMD said.

Rain, wind and surge warnings

In its bulletin issued at 3 p.m. on Wednesday, the IMD said extremely heavy rainfall is likely in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli and Kakinada districts on November 19, with the alert remaining in place for November 20. An orange alert covers Parvathipuram Manyam, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, East Godavari and West Godavari, where isolated very heavy rainfall is likely on November 19 and 20, The Hindu reported.

For Odisha, the IMD has warned of squally winds of 40-50 kmph gusting to 60 kmph along and off the coast, rising to 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph from the night of November 18, and gale-force winds of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph from the morning of November 19 until noon on November 20, Sambad English reported. A storm surge of 0.5 to 1 metre above the astronomical tide could inundate low-lying areas of south coastal Odisha at landfall.

Why this storm is hard to forecast

Forecasters say Akvan has been unusually difficult to track. Unlike earlier systems Arnab and Murasu, whose tracks could be forecast clearly, the eight to nine models meteorologists use to reach a consensus are pointing in different directions this time, P.L.N. Murthy, head of the Cyclone Warning Centre, told The Hindu — which is why the IMD has given a landfall window as wide as Narsapur to Puri.

"No two models are showing the same results. Akvan has become a new case study for us, since we never experienced so much uncertainty."

— P.L.N. Murthy, Head, Cyclone Warning Centre, to The Hindu

The same factors are behind the weakening, Murthy said: El Niño conditions, and a Bay of Bengal that has already seen two systems this season, Arnab and Murasu, leaving insufficient mid-level moisture for a third. The storm first moved towards Machilipatnam, where ocean heat was sufficient, but then travelled further north into colder waters off north coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, where it could not draw the heat and moisture needed to sustain greater intensity.

Preparedness under uncertainty

The uncertain landfall point is also complicating the response. G. Venkata Ramana, a meteorologist at the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority, told The Hindu it was difficult for the government to deploy disaster management teams without knowing the probable landfall points, but that National Disaster Response Force and State Disaster Response Force teams have been kept on standby. More clarity on the track is expected by Wednesday night.
